label: Trino

oidc._jwtAudiencePath: Trino's JWT authenticator (on beside OAUTH2 for programmatic clients such as Superset) accepts only tokens whose audience is this client id (with an External-source security profile, the profile's JWT Audience when set): KDPS writes it here and adds it to the tokens of the clients it registers that call this Trino. Without it any token of the realm authenticates, one issued to another application for a signed-in user included.

catalogEnrichments._description: When KDPS provisions the catalog it names it after the release and namespace, so the rendered Trino catalog must point at that name rather than the one the platform context advertises. Applied here, server-side, because it is the same value the provisioning step derives.
catalogEnrichments.name: iceberg-provisioned-warehouse

variables.comment: OpenShift: worker autoscaling reads metrics from the platform's built-in (user-workload) monitoring via the thanos-querier CLUSTER endpoint (:9091). The KEDA SA is bound to cluster-monitoring-view, so :9091 is the correct port (the :9092 tenancy port returns HTTP 400 for a cluster-view token and needs a per-request namespace param KEDA does not send). Verified on CRC: :9091 + bearer token returns the trino_* metrics. On vanilla K8s the kube-prometheus-stack address above is used instead.
variables.name: keda.thanos.serverAddress

variables.comment: Secret holding a bearer token for a ServiceAccount bound to the cluster-monitoring-view ClusterRole; consumed by the KEDA TriggerAuthentication on OpenShift. Operator-provided (see Cluster prerequisites), defaulting to this convention name.
variables.name: keda.thanos.tokenSecret

variables.comment: true only when Trino does NOT terminate TLS itself. Gates the forwarded-header trust below: with TLS on the coordinator, trusting X-Forwarded-Proto would let anything inside the cluster reach the plain HTTP port and claim the request arrived over TLS — the very check that guards authenticated traffic.
variables.name: tlsHttpsDisabled

bindings.name: ingress-setup
bindings._description: Writes the canonical ingress shape every KDPS chart accepts. The `hosts[]` entry uses the rich object form `{host, paths[]}` so OpenMetadata- and Trino-style charts work out of the box; the Superset chart's template was made shape-tolerant (accepts string OR object) in chart >= 0.12.25.

bindings.name: openshift-route-allowlist
bindings._description: On OpenShift the chart copies ingress.annotations onto its Route; some clusters refuse a Route without this router annotation.

bindings.name: ingress-nginx-tuning
bindings._description: Backslash-escaped dots in the leaf key — the UI binding engine (bindings.ts:pathToParts) treats backslash-dot as a literal dot so the rendered values look like `ingress.annotations: { "nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffer-size": "..." }`.

bindings.name: init-container-resources
bindings.comment: Kubernetes counts init containers when it sets the pod QoS class: the chart's own init containers get requests equal to limits so the coordinator and workers stay Guaranteed.

bindings.name: keda-enable
bindings.comment: server.keda.enabled, minReplicaCount and maxReplicaCount are wizard fields (Autoscaling group).

bindings.name: service-monitor-enable
bindings.comment: serviceMonitor.enabled is the 'Collect metrics' wizard field.

Default (vanilla Kubernetes) KEDA triggers — scrape the kube-prometheus-stack Prometheus directly, no auth. Gated on isVanillaK8s so they are used everywhere EXCEPT a confirmed OpenShift cluster (where the openshift variant below takes over).
bindings.name: keda-triggers

bindings.comment: OpenShift KEDA triggers — same queries, but pointed at the thanos-querier tenancy endpoint (platform user-workload monitoring) with authModes=bearer and an authenticationRef to the TriggerAuthentication below. Gated on isOpenShift (fail-CLOSED: only a confirmed OpenShift cluster).
bindings.name: keda-triggers-openshift

bindings.comment: OpenShift only: turn on the chart's KEDA TriggerAuthentication (bearer token from the SA-token Secret) so the thanos-authenticated triggers above can read platform monitoring.
bindings.name: keda-trigger-auth-openshift

targets.comment: service-ca.crt in the service-account-token Secret is the CA that signs the monitoring endpoint's certificate, so the triggers verify it instead of skipping the check.

Written when internal HTTPS is off too: an upgrade starts from the release's values, which hold true when it was installed with internal HTTPS, so skipping the target above would leave HTTPS on while the options that need it are turned off (kdps-service-user-needs-https).

Flags only. The truststore SECRET is deliberately NOT set from this release's keystore: it is the CA bundle KDPS wires from the platform context (trino-truststore), and repointing it at the server keystore would leave Trino unable to verify the Keycloak JWKS endpoint or Ranger — breaking the very OIDC path TLS is being enabled for.

bindings.comment: Edge-terminated TLS only: Trino then has to believe the router about the original scheme. Skipped once Trino terminates TLS itself — see tlsHttpsDisabled.
bindings.name: trust-proxy-headers

bindings.comment: 'Let KDPS manage catalogs' is a password login, which Trino only accepts over HTTPS: the chart refuses it without internal HTTPS and the dry run fails. The checkbox is on by default and only hidden once internal HTTPS is off, and a hidden field still sends its value, so it is turned off here.
bindings.name: kdps-service-user-needs-https
iceberg-catalog
bindings._description: Trino 'iceberg' catalog on the Platform Context's Apache Polaris REST catalog. The region is written even without an S3 endpoint override: Trino's native S3 filesystem resolves a region when the catalog is constructed, before any table is loaded, so vended credentials do not remove the need for it and the connector fails to start without one. The OAuth2 client credential is NOT written here: the view fills polarisCredential.* and the clemlab-trino chart (>=1.43.9) appends iceberg.rest-catalog.oauth2.credential=${ENV:POLARIS_CLIENT_ID}:${ENV:POLARIS_CLIENT_SECRET} from a Secret — the view interpolator would blank a literal ${ENV:...}.

bindings.name: iceberg-s3-credential-inline
bindings._description: Static S3 keys for a Polaris catalog on a no-STS object store (Ozone S3 gateway / MinIO). The chart (>=1.43.10) exposes them as ICEBERG_S3_ACCESS_KEY/ICEBERG_S3_SECRET_KEY from a Secret, appends s3.aws-access-key/s3.aws-secret-key=${ENV:...} to the iceberg catalog and turns Polaris credential vending off there.

KDPS-provisioned access. The provisioning step runs before the chart is installed: it mints this release's Polaris identity, creates the catalog and bucket named <release>-<namespace> unless creation was turned off, and writes <release>-polaris-credential with client_id/client_secret.
bindings.name: iceberg-provisioned-credentials

bindings._description: The same Secret also carries access_key/secret_key, but the provisioning step writes those two ONLY when the operator supplied a static S3 access key. Pointing the chart at them regardless makes it mount env vars from keys that do not exist, and every pod fails with CreateContainerConfigError before it starts. Gated on the same form field the provisioning step reads.
bindings.name: iceberg-provisioned-s3-credential
hadoop-group-mapping-toggle
bindings._description: Sets hadoopConf.groupMapping.enabled — gates the init-container that splices LdapGroupsMapping into core-site.xml (chart >= 1.43.0).

bindings.name: hadoop-group-mapping-ldap-props
bindings._description: Map every Hadoop LdapGroupsMapping form field to its helm path. All paths under hadoopConf.groupMapping.ldap.* are read by the trino chart's init-hadoop-conf-overlay init container.

form.name: openshiftOptions
form.label: OpenShift
form.help: OpenShift-specific options. Only shown when KDPS detects the cluster is OpenShift.

fields.name: runAsUser
fields.label: Run pods as a specific UID (optional)
fields.help: Leave blank: OpenShift picks a UID from the project's range.
fields.helpMore: Set a UID only if you must pin one. It must fall inside the namespace's openshift.io/sa.scc.uid-range annotation, or admission rejects the pods.

form.name: releaseName
form.label: Release name
form.validationHint: Use at most 53 lower-case letters, digits, '-' and '.', starting and ending with a letter or digit (Helm's rule for release names).

form.name: nameOverride
form.label: Name override
form.help: Appended to the release name to form the full name (e.g. <release>-clemlab-trino).

fields.name: serviceMonitor.enabled
fields.label: Collect metrics (ServiceMonitor)
fields.help: Lets Prometheus scrape the service. Required by worker autoscaling.
fields.helpMore: On OpenShift this needs the monitoring-edit role in the project. To turn it off, turn worker autoscaling off first.

fields.name: monitoring.discovery
fields.label: Discover monitoring stack
fields.help: Finds the Prometheus already on the cluster and fills the fields below.

fields.name: monitoring.namespace
fields.label: Monitoring namespace
fields.help: Namespace of the Prometheus stack, or where KDPS installs one when none is found.

fields.name: monitoring.release
fields.label: Monitoring release (Helm)
fields.help: Helm release of the Prometheus stack.
fields.helpMore: Used to build the Prometheus address when none is given, and set as the release label on the ServiceMonitors.

fields.name: monitoring.url
fields.label: Prometheus address
fields.help: Address the autoscaler queries, filled by discovery. Leave blank to use http://<release>-prometheus.<namespace>.svc:9090.

fields.name: serviceMonitor.enabled
fields.label: Collect metrics (ServiceMonitor)
fields.help: Lets Prometheus scrape Trino. Required by worker autoscaling.

fields.name: monitoring.serviceMonitorLabels
fields.label: ServiceMonitor labels
fields.help: Labels the Prometheus selects ServiceMonitors by, as key=value pairs separated by commas. Filled by discovery.

fields.name: keda.discovery
fields.label: Discover KEDA
fields.help: Finds the KEDA operator already on the cluster, used by worker autoscaling.
fields.helpMore: When none is found, KDPS installs KEDA in the namespace below.

fields.name: keda.namespace
fields.label: KEDA namespace
fields.help: Namespace KDPS installs KEDA into, as no KEDA operator was found.

fields.name: webUi.enabled
fields.label: Enable the web UI
fields.help: Sets web-ui.enabled in Trino (the UI is available by default).

fields.name: ingress.enabled
fields.label: Enable Ingress
fields.help: Expose the service through an Ingress (a Route on OpenShift).
fields.helpMore: Required with an authentication profile (OIDC, LDAP over TLS): sign-in needs a public hostname and HTTPS.

fields.name: ingress.ingressClassName
fields.label: Ingress class
fields.help: Ingress class name (e.g. 'nginx', 'openshift-default'). Leave empty for the default controller.

fields.name: ingress.host
fields.label: Hostname (DNS)
fields.help: Public DNS name of the service, e.g. trino.example.com.
fields.helpMore:
On OpenShift it must sit under the cluster's ingress domain (…apps-<cluster>); leave it blank to let OpenShift assign one.
With OIDC it is also the sign-in redirect (https://<host>/oauth2/callback): register it in the identity provider.

fields.name: ingress.path
fields.label: HTTP path
fields.help: Base path for the Ingress (usually '/').

fields.name: ingress.tlsMode
fields.label: TLS mode
fields.help: Where the service's TLS certificate comes from.
fields.helpMore:
Sign via cert-manager: recommended when cert-manager is installed (renews automatically).
Sign with Company CA: a CA uploaded under Security → Certificate Authorities.
Sign with Ambari Internal CA: for tests, browsers warn.
Modes whose system is not installed are hidden. TLS is required with an authentication profile.
On Upgrade/Config this starts on 'Keep current certificate' (or 'None' for plain HTTP). Pick another mode only to replace the certificate; you are asked to confirm, and a Secret kept by cert-manager or an external store is never overwritten.

options.label: Source from external Secret store (Vault, ESO)
None (HTTP only — not allowed with auth)

fields.name: ingress.tlsSecret
fields.label: Existing TLS Secret name
fields.help: Name of a kubernetes.io/tls Secret already present in the release namespace. The chart references it via ingress.tls[].secretName.

fields.name: ingress.tlsUpload.cert
fields.label: TLS certificate (PEM, leaf + chain)
fields.help: Paste the full chain (leaf first). Saved as tls.crt in the new Secret.

fields.name: ingress.tlsUpload.key
fields.label: TLS private key (PEM)
fields.help: Paste the private key matching the certificate above. Saved as tls.key.

fields.name: ingress.tlsUpload.secretName
fields.label: Target Secret name
fields.help: Secret created from the uploaded certificate. Blank: <release>-ingress-tls.

fields.name: ingress.tlsSelfSign.caName
fields.label: Company CA
fields.help: Company CA that signs the service's certificate.
fields.helpMore: KDPS signs the certificate itself: the CA key never goes to the release's cluster. Upload CAs under Security → Certificate Authorities.

fields.name: ingress.tlsSelfSign.validityDays
fields.label: Leaf validity (days)
fields.help: How long the minted leaf certificate is valid. Capped server-side at 825 (CA/Browser Forum baseline).

fields.name: ingress.certManager.issuerName
fields.label: ClusterIssuer
fields.help: cert-manager issuer that signs and renews the certificate.
fields.helpMore: KDPS writes a Certificate before the install; cert-manager creates the Secret and renews it before it expires.

fields.name: ingress.certManager.validityDays
fields.label: Leaf validity (days)
fields.help: Validity in days. Translated to durationHours on the Certificate resource. cert-manager renews at duration/6 before expiry.

fields.name: ingress.externalSecret.secretStoreName
fields.label: SecretStore
fields.help: Pick an external-secrets SecretStore or ClusterSecretStore. Typically Vault-backed for TLS leaves (PKI mount).

fields.name: ingress.externalSecret.remoteKey
fields.label: Remote key / path
fields.help: Path of the certificate in the external store.
fields.helpMore: Vault PKI: pki/issue/<role>. Vault KV: secret/data/tls/<name>. AWS Secrets Manager: the secret's name.

fields.name: ingress.externalSecret.refreshInterval
fields.label: Refresh interval
fields.help: ESO refresh cadence. e.g. '1h', '15m', '0' (no periodic refresh).

fields.name: ingress.route.ipWhitelist
fields.label: Allowed source IPs (OpenShift Route)
fields.help: Source IPs or CIDRs allowed to reach the Route, space separated. Blank: all.
fields.helpMore: OpenShift only, e.g. 10.0.0.0/8 172.16.20.0/24. Set it when the cluster requires the haproxy.router.openshift.io/ip_whitelist annotation on every Route.

fields.name: ingressTuning
fields.label: Ingress tuning (nginx)

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyBufferSize
fields.label: proxy-buffer-size
fields.help: nginx proxy-buffer-size. Blank: the chart's default.
fields.helpMore: 16k under OIDC, else nginx's default (4k/8k). Raise it on 502 'upstream sent too big header' after sign-in.

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyBuffersNumber
fields.label: proxy-buffers-number
fields.help: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-buffers-number. Total response buffers = number × size.

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyBusyBuffersSize
fields.label: proxy-busy-buffers-size
fields.help: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-busy-buffers-size. Should be ≥ proxy-buffer-size and ≤ total buffer capacity.

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyBodySize
fields.label: proxy-body-size
fields.help: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-body-size. Maximum request body the proxy accepts (e.g. '64m'). Bump for large uploads / file imports.

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyReadTimeout
fields.label: proxy-read-timeout (seconds)
fields.help: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-read-timeout. Bump for long-running queries (Trino, Superset). Default 60.

fields.name: ingress.tuning.proxyConnectTimeout
fields.label: proxy-connect-timeout (seconds)
fields.help: nginx.ingress.kubernetes.io/proxy-connect-timeout. Time the proxy waits when opening a connection to the backend pod.
Advanced nginx settings: usually leave blank.
fields.helpMore: Override them for large OAuth headers, long-running queries or big uploads.

fields.name: tls.https.enabled
fields.label: Enable internal HTTPS
fields.help: Trino serves HTTPS itself. Keep it on.
fields.helpMore:
The keystore is signed by the internal CA; on OpenShift the Route re-encrypts to Trino. Internal clients (Superset, dbt, OpenMetadata) must use https on the HTTPS port.
Turned off, authenticated traffic, tokens included, crosses the pod network in clear text, and 'Let KDPS manage catalogs' is turned off: Trino accepts password logins only over HTTPS.

fields.name: tls.https.autoGenerate
fields.label: Generate the keystore
fields.help: When on, Ambari issues a certificate signed by its internal CA and stores it in a Kubernetes Secret.

fields.name: tls.https.secretName
fields.label: Keystore Secret (optional)
fields.help: Name of the Secret that holds the keystore. Blank: <release>-https.

fields.name: tls.https.password
fields.label: Keystore password
fields.help: Leave blank to generate one.
fields.helpMore: With your own keystore it is kept in the <keystore Secret>-pass Secret. If you created that Secret yourself, it must already hold this password; leave the field blank to keep it.

fields.name: tls.https.keystorePath
fields.label: Path used by Trino
fields.help: Value set as server.config.https.keystore.path.

fields.name: tls.https.keystoreType
fields.label: Keystore format (JKS/PKCS12/PEM)
fields.help: Storage format of the server certificate. PEM creates tls.crt/tls.key/ca.crt.

fields.name: coordinator.resources.requests.cpu
fields.label: CPU request
fields.help: Same as the CPU limit by default. Cannot be higher than the limit.

fields.name: coordinator.resources.requests.memory
fields.label: Memory request
fields.help: Defaults to the memory limit. Cannot exceed it.
fields.helpMore: Equal to the limit, Kubernetes reserves the memory and the pod is among the last evicted when the node runs short. Requests count against the project quota.

fields.name: coordinator.jvm.maxHeapSize
fields.label: Java heap size (optional)
fields.help: Leave blank: 75% of the memory limit, following it.
fields.helpMore: To set it, use the Java format (6G, 6144M) and keep it at 70-80% of the memory limit: Java needs memory outside the heap, and the pod is killed when it goes over the limit.

fields.name: server.workers
fields.label: Number of workers
fields.help: Fixed number of workers (at least 1), used when worker autoscaling is off.

fields.name: worker.resources.requests.cpu
fields.label: CPU request per worker
fields.help: Same as the CPU limit by default. Cannot be higher than the limit.

fields.name: worker.resources.requests.memory
fields.label: Memory request per worker
fields.help: Defaults to the memory limit. Cannot exceed it.
fields.helpMore: Equal to the limit, Kubernetes reserves the memory and workers are among the last evicted. Requests count against the project quota, for every worker autoscaling adds.

fields.name: worker.jvm.maxHeapSize
fields.label: Java heap size per worker (optional)
fields.help: Leave blank: 75% of the memory limit, following it.
fields.helpMore: To set it, use the Java format (6G, 6144M) and keep it at 70-80% of the memory limit: Java needs memory outside the heap, and the pod is killed when it goes over the limit.

fields.name: server.keda.enabled
fields.label: Worker autoscaling
fields.help: Adds and removes workers with the load (KEDA). Off: a fixed number of workers (Worker resources).

fields.name: server.keda.maxReplicaCount
fields.label: Maximum workers
fields.help: Must be at least the minimum.

fields.name: accessControl.type
fields.label: Enable Access Control
fields.help: Disabled lets everyone do everything; Ranger enforces the context's policies.
fields.helpMore: With Disabled, no Ranger repository or plugin is set up.

fields.name: accessControl.properties
fields.label: Access control properties
fields.help: Contents of access-control.properties. Default: allow all.
fields.helpMore: Override it only for another rules provider, such as a file-based one.

fields.name: rangerAdminUrl
fields.label: Ranger admin
fields.help: The Ranger whose policies Trino enforces, from the platform context.

fields.name: tagSync.enabled
fields.label: Sync Atlas tags to Trino
fields.help: Applies the context's Atlas tags to Trino through Ranger tag policies.
fields.helpMore:
Tag-based masking, row filters and access policies then apply to Trino as they do to Hive and Impala. On by default when the context exposes Atlas tags.
KDPS gives the release its own Ranger account for this, kept in the Secret <release>-tagsync-ranger. Ranger lets only administrators write tags, so that account is a Ranger administrator: anyone who can read Secrets in the project can change any Ranger policy with it. Turn this on only where those people may be Ranger administrators.

fields.name: ranger.audit.solrMode
fields.label: Ranger audit to Solr
fields.help: Send Ranger audit events to Solr, shown in Ranger's audit page.
fields.helpMore: 'Follow the platform context' audits to Solr when the context's Ranger does. 'On' and 'Off' decide for this release only.

fields.name: ranger.audit.solrUrls
fields.label: Solr URLs
fields.help: Solr URLs for the audit, comma separated. Blank: the context's.
fields.helpMore: Replaces the context's Solr endpoint, ZooKeeper included.

fields.name: ranger.audit.solrZookeepers
fields.label: Solr ZooKeeper
fields.help: ZooKeeper of a SolrCloud, with its chroot. Blank: the context's.
fields.helpMore: Use it instead of Solr URLs. Replaces the context's Solr endpoint, URLs included.

fields.name: ranger.audit.hdfsMode
fields.label: Ranger audit to HDFS
fields.help: Write Ranger audit events to HDFS files.
fields.helpMore: 'Follow the platform context' audits to HDFS when the context's Ranger does. 'On' and 'Off' decide for this release only. The pods need the cluster's core-site and hdfs-site to reach HDFS.

fields.name: ranger.audit.hdfsDir
fields.label: HDFS audit directory
fields.help: HDFS directory for the audit files, with its file system. Blank: the context's.

fields.name: ranger.audit.log4j
fields.label: Also write Ranger audit to the pod log
fields.help: Also write the audit events to the Trino pod log.

fields.name: hiveCatalog.enabled
fields.label: Enable Hive catalog
fields.help: Adds a 'hive' catalog on the context's Hive Metastore.
fields.helpMore: On by default when the selected context exposes Hive.

fields.name: hiveCatalog.metastoreUri
fields.label: Hive Metastore URI
fields.help: From the platform context. Override only to use another metastore.

fields.name: hive.externalKeytabSecret
fields.label: External Trino service keytab Secret
fields.help: Secret holding Trino's keytab from another realm. Blank: KDPS issues it.
fields.helpMore:
Only for an external context whose KDC KDPS cannot reach (no KDC account on the context). The Secret, in the release namespace, holds key 'service.keytab'. It is Trino's identity for every Kerberos backend: Hive Metastore, HDFS, Ranger.
Create it first: kubectl -n <ns> create secret generic trino-keytab --from-file=service.keytab=./trino.keytab

fields.name: hive.externalKeytabPrincipal
fields.label: External Trino service principal
fields.help: Principal of the keytab above. Blank: the Secret's 'principal' key.

fields.name: hadoopGroupMapping
fields.label: Hadoop LDAP group mapping
fields.help: Reads Hadoop groups from LDAP, for group-based Ranger policies.
fields.helpMore: The Trino container has no SSSD to resolve groups.

fields.name: hadoopConf.groupMapping.enabled
fields.label: Enable LDAP group mapping
fields.help: Adds the LDAP group mapping to core-site.xml at pod start. Chart 1.43.0+.

fields.name: hadoopConf.groupMapping.ldap.url
fields.label: LDAP URL
fields.help: LDAP/IPA endpoint, e.g. ldap://ipa.example.com:389. For LDAPS use ldaps://...:636 and make sure the CA is in Trino's truststore.

fields.name: hadoopConf.groupMapping.ldap.bindUser
fields.label: Bind user
fields.help: DN of the account that reads the directory.
fields.helpMore: FreeIPA hides group membership from anonymous reads. Example: uid=hadoop-group-mapping,cn=users,cn=accounts,dc=example,dc=com

fields.name: hadoopConf.groupMapping.ldap.bindPasswordSecret.name
fields.label: Secret holding the password
fields.help: Secret holding that account's password. Create it first.
fields.helpMore: In the release namespace. Mounted read-only at /etc/hadoop/ldap-bind/password.

fields.name: hadoopConf.groupMapping.ldap.bindPasswordSecret.key
fields.label: Key in the Secret
fields.help: Key of the Secret that holds the password (default 'password').

fields.name: hadoopConf.groupMapping.ldap.baseDn
fields.label: Search base DN
fields.help: Search base for users and groups, e.g. (FreeIPA) cn=accounts,dc=example,dc=com

fields.name: hadoopConf.groupMapping.ldap.userSearchFilter
fields.label: User filter (advanced)
fields.help: {0} is replaced by the user name. Change it only for a non-IPA directory.

fields.name: hadoopConf.groupMapping.ldap.groupSearchFilter
fields.label: Group filter (advanced)
fields.help: LDAP filter that lists the groups. The default works with FreeIPA/RHIDM.

fields.name: hadoopConf.groupMapping.ldap.memberAttr
fields.label: Member attribute (advanced)
fields.help: LDAP attribute holding the DNs of a group's members. FreeIPA: 'member'.

fields.name: hadoopConf.groupMapping.ldap.cacheSeconds
fields.label: Group cache (seconds, advanced)
fields.help: How long the Hadoop client caches resolved groups.

fields.name: hadoopConf.groupMapping.ldap.negativeCacheSeconds
fields.label: Negative cache (seconds, advanced)
fields.help: How long users without groups are cached (spares the directory).

fields.name: icebergCatalog.enabled
fields.label: Enable Iceberg catalog (Polaris REST)
fields.help: Adds an 'iceberg' catalog on the context's Polaris REST catalog.
fields.helpMore: On by default when the context exposes Polaris. On the Polaris side: polaris.realm-context.require-header=false, and its TLS CA in Trino's truststore.

fields.name: icebergCatalog.provision
fields.label: Let KDPS create the catalog and its bucket
fields.help: KDPS creates the catalog and its bucket, named after the release.
fields.helpMore: Reinstalling the release reuses them. Off: nothing is created; KDPS grants this release on the catalog named below.

fields.name: icebergCatalog.restUri
fields.label: Polaris REST catalog URI
fields.help: From the platform context. Override only without an Ambari to resolve it.

fields.name: icebergCatalog.warehouse
fields.label: Polaris catalog (warehouse)
fields.help: Polaris catalog Trino mounts as 'iceberg'.
fields.helpMore: Ignored when KDPS creates the catalog (named after the release and namespace). With creation off, set the catalog to use.

fields.name: icebergCatalog.credentialSecret
fields.label: Existing Polaris credential Secret
fields.help: Secret with a Polaris principal's client_id and client_secret.
fields.helpMore: Optional; takes precedence over the fields below. Create it first: kubectl -n <ns> create secret generic trino-polaris --from-literal=client_id=… --from-literal=client_secret=…

fields.name: icebergCatalog.clientId
fields.label: Polaris client ID
fields.help: Client ID of the Polaris principal Trino uses.
fields.helpMore: Kept in a Secret; the catalog reads it from the environment, never from its ConfigMap.

fields.name: icebergCatalog.clientSecret
fields.label: Polaris client secret
fields.help: OAuth2 client secret of the principal above.

fields.name: icebergCatalog.s3Endpoint
fields.label: Object store (S3 endpoint)
fields.help: Where Iceberg tables are stored: the context's Ozone S3 by default.
fields.helpMore: Override it for another S3-compatible store; leave the override blank for AWS S3 and give credentials below.

fields.name: icebergCatalog.s3Region
fields.label: S3 region
fields.help: Region string sent with S3 requests. Any value works for Ozone; use the real region for AWS S3.

fields.name: icebergObjectStoreOverride
fields.label: Object store override (AWS / other S3)
fields.help: Only for AWS S3 or another S3 store than the context's Ozone.
fields.helpMore: These credentials create the bucket, and go to Trino when the store cannot vend them through Polaris (no STS).

fields.name: icebergCatalog.s3CredentialSecret
fields.label: Existing S3 credential Secret
fields.help: Secret with keys access_key and secret_key. Overrides the fields below.
fields.helpMore: Credential vending through Polaris is then turned off for this catalog.

fields.name: icebergCatalog.s3AccessKey
fields.label: S3 access key
fields.help: Static S3 access key. Stored in a chart-managed Kubernetes Secret and referenced as ${ENV:ICEBERG_S3_ACCESS_KEY}.

fields.name: icebergCatalog.s3SecretKey
fields.label: S3 secret key
fields.help: Secret key matching the access key above.

fields.name: dynamicCatalogs.enabled
fields.label: Allow catalogs to be created at runtime (CREATE CATALOG, no restart)
fields.help: Allows CREATE CATALOG and DROP CATALOG without a restart. Chart 1.43.12+.
fields.helpMore: Ranger authorizes them per user. Catalogs created only at runtime are lost when the pod restarts: define them in this section to keep them.

fields.name: kdps.serviceUser.enabled
fields.label: Let KDPS manage catalogs on the running Trino as the logged-in operator
fields.help: Lets the Catalogs action of the release run as you, under Ranger.
fields.helpMore:
Adds a KDPS login to Trino (a file password user) and grants it 'impersonate' in Ranger, so CREATE/DROP CATALOG run as you. Needs chart 1.43.13+ and 'Enable internal HTTPS'.
With it on, Trino asks every client for a password; without a security profile, kdps is its only login, an administrator. Its password is in the Secret ending in -kdps-service-user (key password).

fields.name: customCatalogs.refs
fields.label: Reusable catalogs
fields.help: Catalogs defined on the Trino Catalogs page, copied into this release.
fields.helpMore: The release keeps that copy until you reapply it from Upgrade/Config. A catalog using ${ENV:KEY} needs the Secret holding KEY under 'Secrets with catalog credentials'.

fields.name: customCatalogs.text
fields.label: Additional Trino catalogs
fields.help: Extra catalogs: a [name] header, then its .properties lines.
fields.helpMore: connector.name is required. The Hive and Iceberg catalogs are configured above, not here. Credentials cannot be inline: reference them as ${ENV:KEY} from a Secret under 'Secrets with catalog credentials'.

fields.name: catalogCredentialSecrets
fields.label: Secrets with catalog credentials
fields.help: Secrets whose keys catalogs reference as ${ENV:KEY}. Chart 1.43.16+.
fields.helpMore:
Every key becomes an environment variable of the Trino pods, e.g. connection-password=${ENV:PG_PASSWORD}; credentials never sit in the catalog ConfigMap or in KDPS. Restart Trino after changing a Secret.
kubectl -n <ns> create secret generic postgres-credentials --from-literal=PG_PASSWORD=…

retiredValues._comment: Values an earlier version of this definition wrote, removed from the values of every deploy (wizard upgrades and redeploys without the wizard alike).
retiredValues.internalSharedSecret: The chart generates the internal shared secret and keeps it in the <fullname>-internal-communication Secret; the operator-typed value is no longer used.

additionalConfigProperties.reason: The internal shared secret written out in the server configuration (a ConfigMap); the chart reads it from its Secret.

coordinator.additionalConfigProperties.reason: The HTTPS keystore password written out in the coordinator configuration (a ConfigMap); the chart's init container appends it from the keystore password Secret.

featureChartVersions._comment: Atlas tag sync renders a tag-projector CronJob that only exists from 1.43.11; on an older chart the toggle would deploy cleanly and do nothing.

secretChartVersions._comment: Chart 1.43.16 reads the security profile's bind password and inline OIDC client secret from a Secret (${ENV:...} in the server configuration); an older chart writes them into the coordinator ConfigMap and plain environment variables. A wizard deploy that carries one of them with an older chart is refused; a resync or a security refresh is warned in its operation log.

platformOps._description: When Atlas tag sync is on and access control is Ranger (the chart runs the projector only then), KDPS creates the release's own Ranger account, kdps-tagsync-<namespace>_<release>_<hash of the KDPS instance, Kubernetes API server and platform context>, on the selected context's Ranger (directly, or through the Ambari server on the managed cluster) with a new password at every deploy, records it in the view, writes only that account into the Secret <release>-tagsync-ranger {user,password} of the release namespace and injects tagSync.ranger.{url,existingSecret} into the values. The context's Ranger administrator credentials never leave KDPS. Ranger lets only ROLE_SYS_ADMIN import tags, so the account is a Ranger administrator for whoever can read Secrets in the namespace. Uninstalling the release, or a deploy that gives the projector no KDPS account (tag sync off, the operator's own Secret, auto-configuration off), disables the recorded account and deletes the Secret, as does a first install that fails or is canceled before the release is installed. Values naming another Secret in tagSync.ranger.existingSecret, or a Secret <release>-tagsync-ranger that KDPS did not write, bring the operator's own account instead: KDPS creates none and never replaces or deletes that Secret.

Trino reads Hive tables as its own service identity (hive.hdfs.trino.principal); the Hive metastore's Ranger plugin therefore authorises that identity, not the end user. Trino cannot read Hive as the end user, so that identity is granted SELECT on the context's Hive repository. Superset's Hive connection impersonates the end user, so its service identity gets no Hive grant; OpenMetadata's ingestion identity is granted by its own base-ingestion step.

securityCoupling.unauthenticatedExposure: Without sign-in Trino trusts the user name each client sends: anyone who reaches this address can run queries as any user, administrators included, and Ranger authorizes that name.

sizing._comment: Sizes offered at step 3 of the wizard. A size fills the listed form fields; M is the fields' defaults. The fields are edited in the sizing dialog instead of the form.
